references.text: Jesus stayed in Samaria for two days after the Samaritans' invitation ([ref:Joh 4:40|John 4:40]). Verse 43 refers back to these two days before he continued on to Galilee.
Earlier in the chapter, Jesus left Judea to go to Galilee ([ref:Joh 4:1-3|John 4:1-3]). Now he completes this journey after his stay in Samaria.

The verse introduces Jesus' arrival in Galilee, and what follows in [ref:Joh 4:44-45|John 4:44-45] explains the context: Jesus himself testified that a prophet is not honored in his own homeland, but the Galileans still welcomed him because they had seen what he did in Jerusalem.
Galilee was the place of Jesus' first sign, the wedding at Cana ([ref:Joh 2:1-2|John 2:1-2]). Jesus' return to Galilee in 4:43 leads to the second sign at Cana (4:46-54).
Jesus' arrival in Galilee leads directly to the healing of the official's son in Cana ([ref:Joh 4:46-54|John 4:46-54]), which is the second sign Jesus performs in Galilee.

Also in the synoptic gospels, Jesus goes to Galilee to begin his public ministry ([ref:Matt 4:12-13|Matthew 4:12-13]). Both traditions show that Galilee was a central starting point for Jesus' service.
